extracted.intended_audience: math content creators and students considering submitting a math explainer video to the Summer of Math Exposition (SoME); educators and anyone interested in producing math exposition videos
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for submitting a math explainer (often animated) video to the Summer of Math Exposition (SoME), including what aspects submissions are judged on and what topics fit the style. Intended for creators preparing a submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed by SoME as one of the aspects submissions are assessed on: "clarity".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further elaboration on this page; the SoME website provides a video with tips on how to create a math explainer which likely expands on achieving clarity. Top submissions (top 20) can be inspected as exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed by SoME as one of the aspects submissions are assessed on: "motivation".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page gives no detailed scoring guidance; creators are pointed to SoME's tips video and example top submissions to see strong motivational approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed by SoME as one of the aspects submissions are assessed on: "novelty".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No explicit definition on this page; novelty likely refers to fresh perspective, unusual topic choice, or original presentation — examine top submissions for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorability
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed by SoME as one of the aspects submissions are assessed on: "memorability".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further details here; use SoME tip resources and exemplar videos to learn techniques that increase memorability (narrative hooks, striking visuals, clear takeaways).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed by SoME as one of the aspects submissions are assessed on: "length".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page does not state preferred durations; creators should consult SoME official site or top submissions to infer appropriate video length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic choice — two categories (usefulness vs. art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoted description from 3Blue1Brown quoted on the page: "Topics tend to fall into one of two categories: Those people might be seeking out, like linear algebra, neural networks, calculus, Fourier transforms, quantum mechanics, etc. Problems in math which many people may not have heard of, and which seem quite challenging at first, but where some shift in perspective makes it both doable and beautiful."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This suggests an implicit criterion for topic selection: pick topics that either (a) are broadly useful and sought-after, or (b) are lesser-known challenging problems that become approachable/beautiful with the right perspective. The page notes the line between these categories is easily blurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format — animated/interactive math exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The page highlights 3Blue1Brown as a YouTube channel focused on discovery/creativity and notes their written lessons often include interactive elements; it also points readers to a SoME video with tips and to the top submissions, and advises those interested in animated content to check the SoME website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit preference or encouragement for clear, possibly animated/visual/explainer formats with interactive or visual elements; creators are directed to review SoME tips and exemplar animated submissions for implementation details.
